To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synthesis of freezing tolerance proteins in wheat is tissue and cultivar dependent.
cold hardening induces important changes in the protein patterns in the leaves, root and crown of wheat, depending on the tissue and cultivars.

(a) cold hardening induced the synthesis of at least eight new proteins in the leaves, the crown, and the roots; and (b) some of these proteins were expressed at a greater level in the freezing-tolerant than in the sensitive cultivars, suggesting a relationship between their synthesis and the degree of cold tolerance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of freezing tolerance proteins during the acclimation of wheat to cold.
the identification of proteins that are induced during the cold acclimation of wheat.
the identification of freezing tolerance proteins in the leaves, roots, and crown of winter wheat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
freezing stress induces the synthesis of a number of new proteins, some of which may have a role in the acquisition and/or maintenance of freezing tolerance.
cold hardening is associated with the accumulation of specific proteins, which are expressed in a tissue-specific manner and which may have an important function in the cellular response to freezing.
the synthesis of proteins is a major component of the cold acclimation process in wheat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
freezing tolerance is a complex phenomenon involving a number of physiological, biochemical, and genetic factors.

cold acclimation of wheat plants induces a complex and tissue-specific pattern of protein synthesis and that some of these newly synthesized proteins are related to the freezing tolerance of the plants.
freezing tolerance is a multigenic trait and is associated with changes in the protein patterns in the three tissues studied.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the freezing tolerance of wheat is associated with the synthesis and accumulation in the leaves, the crown, and the roots of a number of proteins, some of which are expressed at higher levels in the freezing tolerant than in the freezing sensitive cultivars.
the synthesis of freezing tolerance proteins is not restricted to the leaves, but also occurs in the crown, and roots.
the cold acclimation process in wheat induces the synthesis of specific proteins in leaves, crown and roots.
